subject: StrataBank: conditional feature commitment for audit & residency needs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@stratabank.com>, StrataBank Legal <legal@stratabank.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: StrataBank follow-up — residency & audit features for contract cadence

Team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — StrataBank is excited and is moving toward an internal approval window that ends mid‑October. A couple of asks came up from their procurement/legal teams that are deal blockers unless we can commit to a conditional roadmap/timeline:

- Tenant-level audit exports (scheduled bulk export + on-demand) with retention controls.
- EU residency for logs/exports (data-at-rest in EU region + CMK support).
- Ability to opt into stricter redaction options for PII in embeddings pipeline (they suggested a toggle).

I’ve attached the mutual action plan and the RFP snippet that lists their must-haves. High level ask: can Product/Eng (Mina/Markus) confirm whether we can prioritize an MVP for these items that would ship before contract signature (targeting Oct 15), or propose a mitigated delivery plan that keeps the deal moving?

They are willing to agree to a 6–9 month pilot commitment and are open to a modest additional monthly fee for dedicated residency. This is an enterprise strategic account for EMEA — if we can deliver a minimal, well-scoped solution, it buys us expansion rights across several Strata verticals.

Next steps I’m hoping for:
- Product: list of scope items we can commit to and what would be considered post-signing.
- Eng: rough timeline/level of effort (sprint allocation estimate).
- CS: any operational workarounds we can offer immediately.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@stratabank.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StrataBank follow-up — residency & audit features for contract cadence

Thanks Ben — looping in Eng (Markus) and Security (Karthik) for technical feasibility.

Quick clarifying questions to scope an MVP before I sketch a proposal:
1) Audit exports: do they need streaming/real-time audit forwarding, or will scheduled bulk exports (daily/weekly CSV/NDJSON) suffice to start?
2) Residency: is the requirement strictly that all audit logs/exports are stored in an EU region and encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK)? Any additional egress restrictions?
3) Redaction toggle: is this for generation output only or for embedding pipelines + stored vectors?
4) Expected scale: what is their projected QPS or monthly API volume during pilot? Even an order-of-magnitude helps.

MVP idea (initial take):
- Provide scheduled audit export (daily) with configurable retention/format.
- Support EU storage for exports and audit logs with CMK integration as a gating item (might need a security review).
- Implement a redaction preprocessing toggle for embeddings (config flag at tenant level) — ship as opt-in.

Open constraints: full EU residency across all ephemeral caches and runtime traces is significantly more complex and may be post-MVP. We can offer an SLA caveat in the contract that outlines exactly what is resident and what remains global until full rollout.

Ben/Priyom — can you ask Strata which of the above is an absolute deal-breaker vs. negotiable? If they need full runtime residency day-one, that’s a bigger ask.

I’ll draft a one-page decision note with scope and trade-offs after I hear back on the clarifications.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Product Manager, Enterprise
mina@redwood.com
From: Elena Rossi <elena@stratabank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: StrataBank follow-up — residency & audit features for contract cadence

Hi Mina / Ben,

Thanks for the quick follow — apologies for the late reply, procurement ran this morning. Answers below:

1) Audit exports: scheduled daily exports are acceptable as an MVP. We will want the ability to run ad‑hoc exports for legal audits, but that can be a short manual process to start.
2) Residency: we require audit logs and exported data to be stored in the EU (specifically Frankfurt) and encrypted with our CMK. We can accept that some runtime telemetry remains outside EU for the pilot, but we need the exported artifacts and retention controls to be EU-only.
3) Redaction: critical for stored vectors/embeddings — if we cannot redact before persistence, this will be a legal blocker.
4) Scale: pilot estimate ~25k calls/day, peak bursts ~2500 RPS for short windows.

Timeline: legal has said we need a clear product commitment in the MAA (mutual action plan) before our board signs. Target signature date: Oct 15. We understand full runtime residency is heavy — the EU storage + CMK + embedding redaction for persistence would be sufficient for the MAA if you can commit to timelines.

Attached the legal requirements excerpt. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps prioritize.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement, StrataBank
elena@stratabank.com

Attachments: Legal_Reqs.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StrataBank follow-up — residency & audit features for contract cadence

Mina — thanks, scope looks reasonable for an MVP but there are a few engineering caveats to call out:

- Estimated LOE: shipping the three items (daily audit export, EU export storage + CMK wiring, embedding pre-persistence redaction toggle) as an MVP is ~6–8 weeks if we can allocate a focused team (approx. 2 SWE + 1 infra + 1 security engineer full-time). If we cannot dedicate that, timeline stretches to 12+ weeks.
- Technical risks: CMK integration across storage backends requires security sign-off and some infra provisioning in EU region (KMS, storage buckets with restricted network paths). Embedding redaction before persistence touches the inference pipeline and needs validated evals to ensure we don’t regress model utility — plan for a short eval pass.
- Workaround for near-term: we can script daily exports for Strata and provision an EU-only storage bucket for those artifacts (manual operator flow) within ~2–3 weeks. That gives legal something tangible while Eng works on automation.

If Product agrees to the 6–8 week SLA for a committed MVP, we’ll draft a sprint-level plan and resource request. Otherwise we should offer the manual-export interim and include automation timeline in the MAA.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Engineering Lead, Inference Platform
markus@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataBank follow-up — residency & audit features for contract cadence

Appreciate the quick turn, team. To keep the deal moving we need a short, actionable deliverable by EOD Monday (Sep 27) that I can put in the MAA:

1) Mina: one-page summary (scope / in-scope MVP items / out-of-scope) + estimated ship date for automated solution (or range, e.g., 6–8 weeks) and the manual-export interim plan.
2) Markus: high-level resource ask (who we need for the 6–8 week path) + acceptance criteria for the MVP.
3) Priyom: ops/process note for the manual export (who will run it, cadence, SLA of export delivery).

Elena — we’ll include the manual-export interim as an interim mitigation in the MAA and call out the automation timeline we commit to. If Product can commit to the 6–8 week automated MVP we’ll push for the Oct 15 signature.

I’m available to sync 30m today if that helps finalize the one-pager.

Thanks — Ben
